Dayton Readers' Circle Foundation — Early Reading Success Grants (FICTIONAL SAMPLE)
One-year grants for programmes that help children in kindergarten through third grade in Montgomery County read at grade level. Priority for evidence-based tutoring delivered during the school day and for programmes that involve families.
reporting_requirements:
Dayton Readers' Circle Foundation — Interim Report Requirements (FICTIONAL SAMPLE)
An interim report is due at the midpoint of the grant period and a final report within 30 days of its end. Submit as a single PDF to grants@drcf.example.org.
The interim report must include:
1. Progress toward goals (up to 300 words): what was delivered so far and how it compares with the plan in your proposal.
2. Students served (up to 150 words): number of students enrolled to date, schools, and the share starting below benchmark.
3. Early results (up to 250 words): any assessment data available, with the tool you use.
4. Challenges and changes (up to 200 words): anything that did not go as planned and what you changed.
Attach a one-page budget-to-actual report showing spending to date against the approved budget. Photos and a short participant story are welcome but optional.

program_report.title: Programme Progress Report: Fall 2026 (Dayton Readers' Circle grant)
program_report.content:
# Programme Progress Report: Fall 2026

Period covered: September 1 – December 15, 2026. Funded by the Dayton Readers' Circle Foundation ($75,000).

## Delivery
- 286 students in grades K-3 enrolled in One-on-One Tutoring at all nine partner elementary schools in Dayton Public Schools.
- 74% of enrolled students started the year below benchmark on the fall DIBELS 8 assessment.
- 128 trained volunteer tutors completed the six-hour structured literacy training before starting.
- Students received tutoring twice a week for 30 minutes during the school day; average attendance was 87% of scheduled sessions.
- Three Family Reading Nights were held, with 412 family members attending.

## Early results
Winter DIBELS 8 results are due in January. On the mid-fall progress check, 39% of students who started below benchmark had already reached benchmark.

## Challenges
Tutor recruitment at two schools started slowly, so 21 students began tutoring three weeks late. We added a second weekly volunteer orientation, and every waitlisted student was matched by October 6.

## Spending to date
$36,400 of $75,000 spent (49%), mainly on tutor coordinators and books.

> "My son asks to read the bus signs out loud now." — Parent, Westwood Elementary

program_report.title: Family Engagement Report: July – December 2026 (Ohio Valley Community Bank grant)
program_report.content:
# Family Engagement Report: July – December 2026

Funded by the Ohio Valley Community Bank Foundation ($40,000).

## Activities
- Summer Book Bags: every enrolled student took home 10 free books in June and July; 2,860 books were distributed.
- Family Reading Nights: four monthly evening events from September to December at partner schools, teaching simple at-home reading routines.

## People served
- 286 students and 538 family members took part, including 412 family members at Family Reading Nights.

## Volunteers
- 46 volunteers gave 690 hours at Family Reading Nights and book distribution.

## Story
A grandmother raising two first graders came to her first Family Reading Night in September. By November she was leading a reading game at her table for other families.

## Spending to date
$21,300 of $40,000 spent (53%).
